title: DISCIPLINE MEANT TO TURN US BACK

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If in spite of these things you do not accept my correction but
continue to be hostile toward me, I myself will be hostile toward you and
will afflict you for your sins seven times over'" - Lev 26:23-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the crucial word here: correction. God calls all these hardships
His correction, His discipline. The whole purpose was never destruction —
it was to turn His people back to Himself.

This changes how we read the entire warning section. God was not venting
anger. He was doing what a loving parent does with a child running towards
danger — escalating the response, not to harm, but to reach a heart that
would not otherwise listen.

Dear friend, the tragedy in this verse is the phrase "you do not accept my
correction." The discipline was offered as a gift to be received, and they
refused it. Correction only works on a heart willing to be corrected.

Hebrews takes up this exact theme for New Covenant believers: endure
hardship as discipline; God is treating you as His children. He disciplines
us for our good, that we may share in His holiness. No discipline seems
pleasant at the time, but later it produces a harvest of righteousness and
peace for those who have been trained by it (Heb 12:7-11).

That last phrase matters — trained by it. The question is not whether we
face hardship, but whether we let it train us or waste it in resentment.

When difficulty comes, do not immediately assume it is punishment, but do
ask humbly: Father, is there anything You are teaching me here? A teachable
heart turns even hard seasons into growth.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I accept God's correction or resist it?
2. Is there a hard season I have wasted in resentment rather than growth?
3. What might God be gently teaching me right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that Your correction flows from Your love. Give me a
teachable heart that accepts Your discipline and is trained by it, rather
than resisting You. Amen.
